definitions.gloss: without flattery; honestly; in all sincerity
definitions.explanation: A phrase used before a compliment to emphasize that it is genuine and not just polite flattery.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで、おいしいです。
examples.english: Honestly, it's delicious — I'm not just saying that.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで、{素晴|すば}らしいプレゼンでした。
examples.english: Without flattery, it was an excellent presentation.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで{言|い}いますが、{彼女|かのじょ}の{歌|うた}は{本当|ほんとう}に{上手|じょうず}だと{思|おも}います。
examples.english: I'm being completely honest when I say her singing is really good.

notes:
USAGE:
お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで is used to preface a genuine compliment, assuring the listener that the praise is sincere. Japanese social culture involves frequent compliments (お{世辞|せじ}), so this phrase explicitly sets them aside.

VARIATIONS:
- お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きに — slightly more formal variant
- お{世辞|せじ}じゃなく — casual variant (not flattery, but...)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで + praise/compliment
- お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで{言|い}うと... (speaking without flattery...)
